title: Assistant/Associate Professor positions in Computer Science — Nazarbayev University
organization: Nazarbayev University, School of Engineering and Digital Sciences
summary: Faculty positions in Computer Science: AI/ML, data science, cybersecurity and robotics. Internationally competitive package, English-language environment.
role_expected: Teaching plus your own research programme

title: Postdoctoral researcher in Machine Learning — MBZUAI, Abu Dhabi
organization: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence
summary: Postdoc positions across ML, NLP, CV and robotics. A strong publication record (NeurIPS/ICML/ACL level) is expected. Tax-free salary, housing allowance, relocation support.
role_expected: Postdoctoral researcher

title: ML Engineer (Kazakh NLP) — ISSAI, Nazarbayev University
organization: Institute of Smart Systems and AI (ISSAI)
summary: Work on Kazakh speech recognition and large language models (KazLLM ecosystem). PyTorch and multilingual NLP experience required. On-site in Astana.
role_expected: ML engineer

title: Bolashak International Scholarship — 2026 call for PhD studies and research internships
summary: Funds PhD studies and research internships at top world universities. Covers tuition, living costs and travel. For scientists, research internships of up to 12 months.

eligibility.note: Citizens of the Republic of Kazakhstan only

role_expected: Scholarship holder

title: Zhas Galym grant for young scientists — annual call, Ministry of Science and Higher Education RK
organization: Ministry of Science and Higher Education of the Republic of Kazakhstan
summary: Project grants for researchers under 40: projects of up to 3 years across all fields of science, hosted at Kazakhstani universities and research institutes.

eligibility.note: Host organisation must be in Kazakhstan; age limit 40

role_expected: Principal investigator

title: Horizon Europe — MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships 2026
summary: Fellowships of 1–2 years at European host institutions, all disciplines. Any nationality, PhD required, no more than 8 years of research experience.

eligibility.note: Requires moving to a host organisation in the EU or an associated country

role_expected: Fellow

title: Call for Papers: Central Asian Conference on AI & Data Science, Almaty
organization: Central Asian Conference on AI & Data Science
summary: Regional venue for AI/ML and data science. Full papers and posters welcome; a student track is available.
role_expected: Presenting author

title: NeurIPS 2026 — travel grant round-up for students from Central Asia
summary: Every known route to fund the trip: conference financial assistance, the volunteer programme and university travel funds.

eligibility.note: Conditions depend on the specific support programme

role_expected: Attendee

title: Looking for co-authors: survey on NLP for Kazakh and low-resource Turkic languages
summary: A comprehensive survey of datasets, models and benchmarks. Looking for 2–3 co-authors with experience in machine translation, speech, or corpus construction.
role_expected: Co-author of a section

title: Seeking a clinical partner in Kazakhstan for a medical imaging study
summary: Our group works on deep learning for radiology (CT/MRI). We need a hospital or medical university partner for a joint retrospective study and co-supervised student projects.

eligibility.note: Requires an organisation with access to clinical data in Kazakhstan

role_expected: Clinical partner / co-supervisor

title: ERC Starting Grant 2027 — up to €1.5M to build your first research team
summary: The ERC entry-level grant, call ERC-2027-STG, opened on 22 July 2026. Any nationality may apply, but the project must be hosted by an institution in an EU Member State or a country associated to Horizon Europe — from Central Asia this is in practice a relocation grant, and the ERC adds extra funding for exactly that move. The exact years-since-PhD window is set by the ERC Work Programme 2027; check it before you start writing.

eligibility.note: Any nationality; the host institution must be in an EU Member State or a Horizon Europe Associated Country

funding_amount: Up to €1.5M over 5 years, plus up to €1M extra — up to €2M when relocating from a non-associated third country
role_expected: Principal Investigator of your own five-year project

title: ERC Consolidator Grant 2027 — up to €2M to consolidate an independent group
summary: For researchers who already lead their own line of work and want to consolidate it. The 2027 call opens on 24 September 2026 and closes on 12 January 2027. As with all ERC grants, nationality is unrestricted but the host institution must sit in an EU Member State or an Associated Country. The ERC has tightened its 2027 rules: one proposal per applicant under the 2027 Work Programme, and no repeat applications for Starting or Consolidator Grants.

eligibility.note: Any nationality; the host institution must be in an EU Member State or a Horizon Europe Associated Country

funding_amount: Up to €2M over 5 years, plus up to €1M extra — up to €2M when relocating from a non-associated third country
role_expected: Principal Investigator of your own five-year project

title: MSCA Doctoral Networks 2026 — join a European doctoral training consortium
summary: €593 million for over 130 international doctoral networks, training around 1,950 doctoral candidates. Organisations apply as a consortium, not individuals — so this is an entry point for a group that can offer secondments, supervision or a non-academic placement. Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Azerbaijan and Mongolia are third countries automatically eligible for EU funding; Georgia and Armenia are associated to Horizon Europe. The call opened on 28 May 2026.

eligibility.note: Your organisation joins a consortium; the coordinator must be in an EU Member State or Associated Country

funding_amount: €593M across the call; a network funds four-year doctoral training for its recruits
role_expected: Beneficiary or associated partner in a consortium — supervision, secondments or training

title: COST Open Call 2026 — join a European research network (no research budget, but the doors open)
summary: COST funds networking, not research: meetings, short-term scientific missions, training schools and conference grants across a four-year Action. Submission opened 31 July 2026 and the collection closes 28 October 2026. Read the restriction carefully — a proposal needs at least seven COST Full or Cooperating Members, at least half of them Inclusiveness Target Countries, and at least 40% young researchers. An institution from Central Asia or the Caucasus joins as an International Partner Country participant and does not count toward those seven. Up to 80 new Actions will be approved.

eligibility.note: You can join a proposal as an International Partner Country participant, but you cannot count toward the seven required COST Member countries, and COST does not fund the research itself

funding_amount: Networking costs only — COST does not fund research
role_expected: Proposer or participant in a four-year Action

title: Erasmus+ Capacity Building in Higher Education — €200k to €1M for a university partnership
summary: The main EU instrument for modernising universities outside Europe, and the one where all nine QIST countries are eligible — Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan under Region 6 (Central Asia), Armenia, Azerbaijan and Georgia under Region 2 (Neighbourhood East), Mongolia under Region 5 (Asia). Three strands: access to cooperation (€200k–400k), partnerships for transformation (€400k–800k) and structural reform (€600k–1M). The annual deadline is 10 February, 17:00 Brussels time; confirm the 2027 date against the call fiche when it is published.

eligibility.note: Applied for by institutions, not individuals; a consortium needs partners from EU Member States and from the eligible region

role_expected: Applicant or partner institution in a capacity-building consortium
source_name: Erasmus+ Programme Guide — Capacity Building in Higher Education

title: Faculty for the Future 2027–2028 — PhD and postdoc grants for women in STEM
summary: For women from low and middle income countries doing a PhD or postdoc at a university abroad, with a commitment to return home and build STEM capacity there. Applications opened 1 September 2026 and close 7 November 2026 at 12:00 noon CST; reference letters are due 14 November. Dual citizenship of a high-income country disqualifies. The eligible-country list matters here more than usual: we checked it for the nine QIST countries and only Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Turkmenistan are on it.

eligibility.note: Women only; you must already be enrolled or admitted at a host university abroad and commit to returning home
eligibility.countries_source_name: Schlumberger Foundation — Faculty for the Future eligibility criteria

funding_amount: Stated in the call documents — we have not verified an amount from the primary source
role_expected: PhD candidate or postdoctoral researcher at a host university abroad
source_name: Schlumberger Foundation — Faculty for the Future

title: Humboldt Research Fellowship — 6 to 24 months of research in Germany
summary: Open to researchers of any nationality except German, in any discipline, with a confirmed host in Germany. Postdocs need a doctorate from the last four years and receive €3,000 a month; experienced researchers with a doctorate from the last twelve years receive €3,600. You must not have spent more than 90 days in Germany in the 18 months before applying. There are three rounds a year — 15 March, 15 July and 15 November — and a round closes early once 800 applications arrive. The current round is full; the next opens 15 November 2026. Roughly 20–25% of applications succeed.

eligibility.note: Any nationality except German; you need a confirmed German host institution before you apply

role_expected: Research stay with a host institute in Germany

title: TWAS–FAPESP Postdoctoral Fellowship — up to 12 months in São Paulo, Brazil
organization: UNESCO-TWAS and FAPESP (São Paulo Research Foundation)
summary: Postdoctoral fellowships in São Paulo state across the natural, applied and social sciences, starting August 2027. You need a doctorate obtained within the last seven years, no residence visa in Brazil or a developed country, and acceptance from a supervisor at a São Paulo university. Watch the two-stage timing: the supervisor submits an expression of interest by 1 November 2026, the list of eligible supervisors appears on 1 December 2026, and full proposals are due 1 April 2027. Eligibility follows the TWAS developing-countries list, which includes all five Central Asian republics, Azerbaijan and Mongolia — but not Georgia or Armenia.

eligibility.note: Doctorate within the last seven years; you must secure a São Paulo supervisor before the expression-of-interest date

funding_amount: Stated in the call for proposals document
role_expected: Postdoctoral researcher at a São Paulo state university

title: NATO Science for Peace and Security — grants where all nine QIST countries are partners
organization: NATO Science for Peace and Security Programme
summary: One of the few international schemes where every QIST priority country is an eligible partner: Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, the Kyrgyz Republic, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Azerbaijan, Georgia, Armenia and Mongolia are all on the NATO partner list. SPS funds multi-year projects, advanced research workshops and advanced training courses, always led jointly by a co-director from a NATO member country and one from a partner country, on security-related priorities. Up to three calls open per year and proposals go through the SPS grant platform — check the SPS page for the call that is open now.

eligibility.note: A proposal needs two co-directors — one from a NATO member country, one from a partner country — and must address an SPS key priority

funding_amount: Multi-year projects above €400,000 need prior approval; workshops and training courses are smaller
role_expected: Co-director of a project, workshop or training course
source_name: NATO — Science for Peace and Security grants

title: IIE Scholar Rescue Fund — visiting academic positions for threatened scholars
summary: Fellowships that place professors, researchers and public intellectuals whose life or work is under threat into temporary visiting positions at universities outside their home country. Listed by UNESCO-TWAS among its external opportunities with a deadline of 11 October 2026. This is not a research grant: it is a safety mechanism, and it is here because a directory of researchers should carry it.

eligibility.note: For scholars facing threats to their life, liberty or academic career; a host institution is arranged as part of the fellowship

funding_amount: Visiting academic position with a stipend, arranged with the host institution
role_expected: Visiting scholar at a host university
